patterns.name: Past-time-marker + bare irregular verb (đã-drop, irregular whitelist)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese marks past with the optional particle 'đã' and never inflects the verb ('Hôm qua tôi đi' = 'Yesterday I go'). Learners carry the uninflected verb into English even when a past time marker is present.
patterns.fp_risk_note: Live rule fires only for subject + {buy,do,eat,go,have} + a beginner past marker, and is blocked by question-like surfaces. Negatives stress: (1) habitual present with 'every day' (no past shift), (2) future 'tomorrow' context, (3) already-correct past form (no double-tensing).

negative.expectedCorrection: Every day I go to school.

liveEngine.corrected: Every day I go to school.

negative.notes: Habitual present; no past marker -> must abstain. Verified abstains.
Future context; must not past-shift. Verified abstains.
Already correct past; no double-tensing. Verified abstains.

patterns.name: Past-time-marker + bare REGULAR verb (đã-drop, -ed insertion)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Same đã-drop transfer, but with regular verbs needing -ed. The live irregular rule's whitelist (buy/do/eat/go/have) does not cover watch/finish/play/cook etc., so these slip through uncorrected.
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk. Naive '-ed on bare verb after past marker' over-fires on: (1) habitual present with frequency adverbs, (2) verbs already in past ('played'), (3) irregulars that must not take -ed ('go'->'goed'), (4) -y/-e spelling shifts (study->studied, like->liked). A safe v1 needs a regular-verb whitelist + spelling map + the same habitual/future blockers the irregular rule uses. Negatives below lock those surfaces.

negative.notes: Habitual present; must not -ed. Verified abstains (and must keep abstaining after wiring).
Already past; no double-ed. Verified abstains.

patterns.name: Future time marker + bare verb (sẽ-drop)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese future particle 'sẽ' is frequently dropped; the verb stays bare ('Ngày mai tôi đi' = 'Tomorrow I go'). Learners produce 'Tomorrow I go' for an intended future.
patterns.fp_risk_note: MEDIUM-HIGH risk. Future-marker + present can be a legitimate scheduled/timetable present ('Tomorrow the store opens at 9'). A safe v1 should restrict to pronoun subjects + a closed future-marker whitelist (tomorrow / next week / next month) + bare lexical verb, and insert 'will' rather than 'be going to'. Must not touch sentences that already contain will/'ll/going to. Negatives lock those.

patterns.name: Completive 'already' + bare verb -> present perfect (rồi-transfer)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese completive 'rồi' / 'đã ... rồi' is rendered as English 'already' but the verb stays in base form ('Tôi ăn rồi' = 'I already eat'). Target is present perfect 'I have already eaten'.
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk. 'already' is grammatical with simple present for stative/cognitive verbs ('I already know', 'She already has it'). A safe v1 must (1) exclude stative verbs (know/have/want/like), (2) require a dynamic lexical verb, (3) emit have/has + past participle (needs a participle map incl. irregulars), (4) skip sentences already in perfect. Negatives lock the stative + already-perfect surfaces.

positive.proposedCorrection: She has already finished her homework.
We have already seen that movie.
positive.notes: GAP. see -> have already seen (irregular participle).

negative.notes: Stative 'know' is fine with simple present + already. Must abstain. Verified abstains.
Already perfect; no re-wrap. Verified abstains.

buildQueuePlacement.rationale: already/present-perfect gap; needs irregular/regular participle whitelist

patterns.name: Adjective predicate copula drop, no intensifier (là-only transfer)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese adjectives are stative verbs needing no copula ('Tôi mệt' = 'I tired'); 'là' is used only before noun predicates. Learners drop 'be' before predicate adjectives. The live 'en-be-verb-omission' rule only fires when 'very' is present, so the bare 'I tired' form is uncovered.
patterns.relatedLiveRule: en-be-verb-omission (requires 'very'; this proposal extends to the no-intensifier case)
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk. 'pronoun + word' is ambiguous: the word may be a base verb ('I sleep', 'She runs') which must NOT take 'be'. A safe v1 requires the predicate to be on a closed adjective whitelist (tired/happy/sad/busy/hungry/cold/hot/sick...) disjoint from the verb lexicon, mirroring en-be-verb-omission's adjective set minus the 'very' requirement. Negatives lock the bare-verb confusables.

positive.notes: GAP. They -> are busy, trailing 'today' kept.

negative.notes: 'sleep' is a verb, not an adjective; inserting 'be' would be wrong. Must abstain. Verified abstains.
Inflected verb; no copula. Must abstain. Verified abstains.
Already has copula; no double-be. Verified abstains.

buildQueuePlacement.rationale: high-frequency VN predicate-adjective transfer; requires adjective whitelist and intensifier guard

patterns.name: Locative copula drop (ở-transfer)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese locative 'ở' carries the predicate alone ('Tôi ở nhà' = 'I at home'), so learners drop 'be' before place phrases. Live rule en-step6-location-be-drop already handles a narrow pronoun + whitelisted-place subset.
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk per the live rule's own note: be-insertion misfires on questions, noun-postmodifier fragments, and clauses with an existing finite verb. The live whitelist covers 'at home / at school / at the office' with pronoun subjects and NO trailing adverb; it abstains on 'the park', 'in the kitchen', noun subjects, and a trailing 'now'. Positives below are the FIRING subset (lockable now); the abstaining extension targets are listed in extensionTargets.

patterns.name: Progressive 'be' drop (đang-transfer)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese progressive particle 'đang' attaches to the bare verb with no auxiliary ('Tôi đang làm' = 'I working'). Learners produce '-ing' with no 'be': 'I working now'.
patterns.fp_risk_note: MEDIUM-HIGH risk. A bare '-ing' word can be a gerund subject/object ('Working is hard', 'I like working') or a reduced relative ('the man working there'). A safe v1 requires pronoun subject + immediately-following present participle + no other finite verb, and inserts am/is/are by person. Negatives lock gerund and already-correct surfaces.

negative.notes: Simple present habitual; no progressive intended. Must abstain. Verified abstains.
Already has auxiliary; no double-be. Verified abstains.

buildQueuePlacement.rationale: progressive be-drop gap; scope to subject + verb-ing surfaces

patterns.name: Adjective placed after noun (noun+adj transfer)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese is head-initial in the noun phrase: the adjective follows the noun ('áo đỏ' = 'shirt red', 'nhà to' = 'house big'). Learners produce 'a shirt red' for 'a red shirt'.
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk. Postnominal adjectives are valid in English ('something red', 'the people responsible', 'time available') and many noun+noun sequences are compounds, not noun+adj. A safe v1 needs both a closed colour/size adjective whitelist AND a concrete-count-noun whitelist, must require an article before the noun ('a shirt red'), and must exclude indefinite pronouns (some/any/no/every + -thing/-one). Negatives lock the postnominal-OK and already-correct surfaces.

positive.notes: GAP. Reorder car new -> new car (also exposes 3rd-person 'buy'->'buys' co-fire; proposedCorrection shows the fully-correct target).

negative.notes: Already correct adj+noun order. Must abstain. Verified abstains.
Predicative adjective (copula complement); NOT a misordered attributive. Must abstain. Verified abstains.

buildQueuePlacement.rationale: noun-adjective order gap; needs noun/adjective whitelist to avoid names/titles

patterns.name: Topic-comment fronting (object/topic fronted before subject)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese is a topic-prominent language: the topic is fronted ('Quyển sách này tôi thích' = 'This book I like'). Learners front the object/topic in English without resumption or relativization.
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk. Topicalization and fronting ARE grammatical in English ('This book, I like'; 'That, I cannot accept'). The live rule sidesteps the risk by matching only three hard-coded exact sentences ('this book i like', 'english i study every day', 'in my family, my mother i love very much') — so it is effectively un-generalizable and brittle. Lockable today ONLY for those exact strings; any generalization needs careful FP work. Positives below are the live rule's exact-match surfaces.
patterns.verifyBeforeLock: All three exact strings captured verbatim from the live engine below; lockable as-is. Note the live regex is lowercase-literal — the engine capitalizes the first letter on output.

patterns.name: Time adverb placed mid-sentence (between subject and verb)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese time adverbs commonly sit between subject and verb ('Tôi hôm qua đi học' is acceptable ordering); learners produce 'I yesterday went to school' instead of fronting or ending the adverb.
patterns.fp_risk_note: MEDIUM risk per the live rule's note: it abstains on frequency adverbs, noun subjects, and multi-clause sentences, only rewriting pronoun + whitelisted time expr + single verb phrase. Observed: only 'I yesterday went...' fired; 'We yesterday played...' and 'He yesterday ate...' ABSTAINED, so the whitelist is extremely narrow (subject/verb-specific). Lock the firing subset; extension targets listed.

patterns.name: Yes/no question missing do-support (intonation-question transfer)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Vietnamese forms yes/no questions with sentence-final particles ('...không?') or rising intonation, never with subject-aux inversion or do-support. Learners produce 'You like coffee?' for 'Do you like coffee?'.
patterns.relatedLiveRule: en-question-form-final-mark (only adds '?' when an aux/be already fronts the clause; does NOT insert do-support)
patterns.fp_risk_note: HIGH risk. Inserting do/does/did requires (1) no existing auxiliary/be/modal, (2) a lexical main verb, (3) correct person/tense agreement on the inserted auxiliary AND base-form reduction of the main verb ('She have a car?' -> 'Does she have a car?'). A safe v1 should require a trailing '?' (the interference signal), a pronoun/simple-NP subject, and a non-aux lexical verb. Negatives lock already-aux questions and plain statements.

negative.notes: Already has do-support; must abstain. Verified abstains.
No '?' -> a statement, not a question. Must abstain (do not turn statements into questions). Verified abstains.

buildQueuePlacement.rationale: high-frequency intonation-question transfer; must stay distinct from final-question-mark rule

patterns.name: Inverted question missing final '?' (already fires)
patterns.vietnameseRoot: Adjacent question-formation surface: when learners DO front an auxiliary/be, they often omit the '?' (Vietnamese leans on the particle, not punctuation). Live rule en-question-form-final-mark repairs this.
patterns.fp_risk_note: Fires for clauses fronted by a be/aux/modal (Are/Is/Do/Can...) lacking terminal '?'. 'Have you eaten' ABSTAINS (perfect aux not in the trigger set), confirming the trigger is a closed set. Negatives lock already-punctuated questions and ensure statements are not interrogated.

negative.notes: Already punctuated; must abstain. Verified abstains.
No fronted aux/be -> a statement; must not add '?'. Verified abstains. (Cross-links QF-1: the do-support form is the real fix here.)
